items.followUp: Differentiate between a population and an ecosystem.

rubric.why: A population consists of organisms of the same species living in a particular area.
rubric.description: Defines a population as members of one species in an area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the same-species group and its area.

rubric.why: A community consists of populations of different species living together in an area.
rubric.description: Defines a community as different populations living in the same area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the different populations or species and their shared area.

modelAnswer: A population is a group of organisms of the same species living in a particular area at a particular time.
A community consists of populations of different species living together in a particular area.

items.followUp: Name two Mendelian laws of inheritance.

rubric.why: The law of segregation is an example of a biological law.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the law of segregation.

rubric.why: The law of independent assortment or the law of dominance is another example of a biological law.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a biological law other than the one already credited.

items.followUp: What is meant by species diversity?

rubric.why: Biodiversity refers to the variety of living organisms or species.
rubric.description: States that biodiversity is variety among living organisms or species.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying variety or diversity of organisms.

rubric.why: The variety is considered within an area, region, ecosystem, or across Earth.
rubric.description: Places that variety in a defined area or on Earth.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating where the variety occurs.

modelAnswer: Biodiversity is the variety of living organisms and species found in an area or on Earth.

items.followUp: What do the terms habitat and niche mean?

rubric.why: Flora refers to the plants of a particular area.
rubric.description: Identifies flora as the plants of an area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that flora means plant life.

rubric.why: Fauna refers to the animals of a particular area.
rubric.description: Identifies fauna as the animals of an area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that fauna means animal life.

modelAnswer: Flora refers to the plant life of a particular area.
Fauna refers to the animal life of a particular area.

items.followUp: What is the function of the plasma membrane?

rubric.why: Cell membrane and plasma membrane are two names for the same structure.
rubric.description: States that the terms are synonyms, not different membranes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explicitly stating that there is no difference or that the terms refer to the same membrane.

rubric.why: The membrane forms the cell's boundary and regulates movement of substances across it.
rubric.description: Gives a feature or function of the shared membrane.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it surrounds the cell or is selectively permeable.

modelAnswer: There is no difference: cell membrane and plasma membrane are two names for the same membrane.
It surrounds the cell and is selectively permeable, controlling the movement of substances into and out of the cell.

items.followUp: Write two differences between mitosis and meiosis.

rubric.why: Mitosis involves one division and produces two daughter cells, whereas meiosis involves two divisions and produces four.
rubric.description: Compares the number of divisions and resulting daughter cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct contrast in divisions or daughter-cell number.

rubric.why: Mitosis maintains chromosome number and usually produces identical cells; meiosis halves chromosome number and produces genetically varied cells.
rubric.description: Compares chromosome number or genetic similarity of the daughter cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct contrast in chromosome number or genetic variation.

modelAnswer: Mitosis consists of one division and produces two daughter cells; meiosis consists of two divisions and produces four daughter cells.
Mitosis maintains the chromosome number and produces genetically identical cells; meiosis halves the chromosome number and produces genetically varied cells.

items.followUp: Describe what happens during the G1 phase of the cell cycle.

rubric.why: DNA is replicated during S phase.
rubric.description: States that DNA replication takes place in S phase.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying DNA replication or doubling as an S-phase event.

rubric.why: G2 follows S phase; the cell continues growing and prepares for mitosis, including synthesizing needed proteins.
rubric.description: States a correct G2 event or its position in the cycle.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying cell growth, preparation for mitosis, protein synthesis, or G2's position after S phase.

modelAnswer: During S phase, DNA is replicated, so the amount of DNA doubles.
During G2 phase, the cell continues to grow and prepares for mitosis by making materials needed for cell division.

items.followUp: What is crossing over, and during which stage of meiosis does it occur?

rubric.why: Chiasmata are the visible points where homologous non-sister chromatids cross and exchange genetic material.
rubric.description: Identifies chiasmata as chromatid crossing or exchange points.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the points of crossing or genetic-material exchange.

rubric.why: Chiasmata form between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes during prophase I of meiosis.
rubric.description: Identifies the chromosomes or chromatids involved, or gives the meiotic stage.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming homologous chromosomes/non-sister chromatids or prophase I.

modelAnswer: Chiasmata are the points where non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes cross over and exchange genetic material.
They form during prophase I of meiosis.
